description: Aerospace Village focuses on aviation and space cybersecurity, satellite reverse engineering, avionics CAN and ARINC bus protocols, GPS and ADS-B spoofing, and Hack-A-Sat challenges.

talks.title: True Story: Hackers in the Aerospace Sector
talks.teaser: Aerospace cybersecurity practitioners and government leaders discuss career paths, working across airlines and federal agencies, and demystifying aviation security.
talks.summary:
Breaking into Aerospace Cybersecurity

While the aerospace sector is traditionally perceived as heavily bureaucratic and closed, government agencies and commercial airlines actively recruit cybersecurity researchers.

Perspectives from Across the Industry

Panelists from commercial aviation, academic institutions, and federal regulatory bodies share personal journeys transitioning into aerospace cyber defense.

Navigating Regulatory and Operational Hurdles

The discussion explores the unique balance between mission assurance, airworthiness certifications, and rapid security vulnerability disclosure.

Building an Inclusive Aviation Security Community

The panel provides actionable advice and mentorship resources for students and researchers looking to apply their skills to aircraft and space systems.

talks.title: Federal Perspective on Aerospace Cybersecurity
talks.teaser: FAA Chief Information Security Officer Larry Grossman shares federal perspectives on securing IT and operational systems across national civil aviation.
talks.summary:
The Evolving Threat Landscape in Civil Aviation

Modern air transportation integrates complex digital systems—from air traffic management backbones to onboard passenger connectivity—expanding the federal cyber attack surface.

FAA Cybersecurity Strategy and Oversight

Larry Grossman and Steve Luczynski discuss how the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) structures cybersecurity defense and regulatory oversight across commercial airspace.

Balancing System Modernization with Legacy Resiliency

Grossman reviews the challenges of securing decades-old avionics protocols while simultaneously deploying cloud-based NextGen flight tracking infrastructure.

Strengthening Public-Private Aviation Collaboration

The speakers emphasize collaborative initiatives between government regulators, airline operators, and independent researchers to harden aviation systems.

talks.title: Fuzzing NASA Core Flight System Software
talks.teaser: Ronald Brobert applies American Fuzzy Lop (AFL) to NASA's Core Flight System (cFS), discovering memory corruption bugs in lunar lander and satellite telemetry apps.
talks.summary:
The Architecture of NASA's Core Flight System

NASA’s Core Flight System (cFS) is an open-source flight software framework deployed on flagship space missions, including the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter and Parker Solar Probe.

Targeting Spacecraft Command and Telemetry Modules

Ronald Brobert investigates key cFS applications, including Command Ingest (CI_Lab) and Telemetry Output (TO_Lab), which process mission commands.

Instrumenting and Fuzzing Spacecraft Software with AFL

Brobert demonstrates setting up American Fuzzy Lop (AFL) test harnesses to fuzz cFS message decoders, discovering multiple buffer overflows and crash conditions.

Hardening Open-Source Flight Software for Space Missions

The author provides remediation patches and automated fuzzing workflows to help flight software engineers validate mission-critical payloads before launch.

talks.title: Collecting CANs: A Bridge Less Travelled
talks.teaser: Pearce Barry revives hardware bridging tools in Metasploit, connecting CAN bus and serial hardware interfaces directly into avionics attack surfaces.
talks.summary:
Revisiting Non-Ethernet Hardware Bridging

While enterprise penetration testing focuses heavily on Ethernet and TCP/IP, avionics and automotive platforms rely primarily on Controller Area Network (CAN) and ARINC serial buses.

Revitalizing the Metasploit Hardware Bridge

Pearce Barry examines the evolution of hardware bridge extensions in Metasploit, illustrating how to route offensive payloads through CAN transceivers and hardware adapters.

Analyzing Aerospace Controller Area Networks

Barry demonstrates packet capture, frame crafting, and command injection across aviation-specific CAN implementations used in general aviation and UAVs.

Building Standardized Hardware Tooling for Aerospace Pentesting

The author shares open-source scripts and hardware configurations to facilitate repeatable security testing on non-Ethernet avionics architectures.

talks.title: Don't Fear the BUS, It Won't Run You Over: Aircraft Avionics 101
talks.teaser: Nicholas Childs demystifies aircraft avionics communication buses, providing a foundational primer on ARINC 429, MIL-STD-1553, and cockpit data networks.
talks.summary:
Introduction to Aircraft Avionics Bus Architectures

Modern aircraft rely on specialized, fault-tolerant serial data buses to interconnect flight control computers, navigation sensors, and cockpit multi-function displays.

Deconstructing ARINC 429 and MIL-STD-1553

Nicholas Childs provides a clear technical breakdown of standard avionics protocols, explaining word formats, parity bits, and point-to-point physical layers.

Expanding Networks into Vulnerable Aircraft Zones

Childs traces how modern digital aircraft architectures bridge once-isolated safety-critical avionics buses with passenger Wi-Fi and maintenance gateways.

A Beginner's Roadmap for Aerospace Protocol Research

The presentation equips researchers with essential hardware sniffers, decoding tools, and safety considerations for analyzing avionics data streams.

talks.title: VDP in Aviation: Experiences and Lessons Learnt
talks.teaser: Matt Gaffney recounts reporting critical vulnerabilities to aircraft manufacturers, analyzing why safety arguments are required to prompt aviation remediation.
talks.summary:
Navigating Vulnerability Disclosure in the Aviation Industry

Disclosing software vulnerabilities in commercial aviation involves unique cultural and regulatory dynamics where standard CVSS severity scores often fail to prompt action.

The 'Features vs. Vulnerabilities' Mindset

Matt Gaffney reflects on disclosing vulnerabilities to an aircraft manufacturer in 2019, discovering that vendors frequently dismiss flaws unless direct airworthiness impact is proven.

Framing Cybersecurity in Terms of Passenger Safety

Gaffney explains how security researchers must translate technical findings (e.g. memory corruption) into measurable flight safety impacts to engage aviation engineers.

Recommendations for Modernizing Aviation VDPs

The author provides guidelines for both researchers and aerospace manufacturers to establish constructive, transparent coordinated disclosure pipelines.

talks.title: Hacking Legacy IFEC in Old Boeing 747s
talks.teaser: Pen Test Partners researchers Alex Lomas and Phil Eveleigh audit legacy In-Flight Entertainment (IFEC) systems decommissioned from retired Boeing 747 aircraft.
talks.summary:
Auditing Retired Commercial Aircraft Hardware

When airlines retire iconic aircraft like the Boeing 747, decommissioned avionics and In-Flight Entertainment and Connectivity (IFEC) systems become available for security research.

Hardware Teardown and Windows NT 4 Exploitation

Alex Lomas and Phil Eveleigh dissect legacy IFEC seatback server racks, uncovering vintage Windows NT 4 operating systems and unencrypted maintenance ports.

Evaluating Passenger-to-Avionics Isolation Boundaries

The researchers evaluate physical and logical network separation, verifying that legacy IFEC servers remain strictly air-gapped from safety-critical flight control buses.

Responsible Disclosure and Decommissioning Practices

The presentation emphasizes that even retired aircraft hardware requires coordinated disclosure and proper data sanitation prior to scrap disposal.

talks.title: Holistic View of a Flight with Crowdsourced Data
talks.teaser: Allan Tart demonstrates combining crowdsourced ADS-B telemetry and VHF air traffic control voice feeds to construct comprehensive real-time flight profiles.
talks.summary:
The Power of Crowdsourced Aviation Telemetry

Global networks of amateur radio receivers and flight tracking aggregators capture vast amounts of unencrypted aviation telemetry transmitted over public airwaves.

Correlating ADS-B Telemetry and VHF Voice Communications

Allan Tart illustrates methodologies for synchronizing raw Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) position data with LiveATC VHF radio feeds.

Constructing Complete Multi-Dimensional Flight Profiles

By cross-referencing flight trajectory telemetry with air traffic control voice instructions, researchers can reconstruct anomalous flight events and route diversions.

Applications for Aviation Safety and Security Analytics

Tart discusses how open-source aviation intelligence enables independent safety auditing, flight route optimization, and detection of navigation spoofing.

talks.title: Steal This Drone: High-Assurance Cyber Military Systems
talks.teaser: Darren Cofer presents outcomes from DARPA's HACMS program, building provably secure military drone flight control software using seL4 microkernels and formal verification.
talks.summary:
The Vulnerability of Military Embedded Systems

Unmanned military platforms and autonomous drones traditionally suffer from memory corruption and architectural vulnerabilities that expose flight controls to remote hijacking.

DARPA High-Assurance Cyber Military Systems (HACMS)

Darren Cofer details Collins Aerospace's leadership in the DARPA HACMS program, developing mathematically verified software and architectures for autonomous aircraft.

Leveraging seL4 Microkernels and Formal Verification

The team utilized the formally verified seL4 microkernel and AADL architecture models, mathematically proving the impossibility of buffer overflows and thread deadlocks.

Red Team Penetration Testing Validation

Cofer recounts extensive adversarial red teaming where elite offensive teams were granted root access to non-critical partitions but were unable to compromise flight controls.

talks.title: Threat Modeling for Space Hitchhikers: CubeSats & Launch Integration
talks.teaser: Oxford researcher James Pavur evaluates cybersecurity threats in secondary rocket payloads, modeling space-to-space radio attacks and CubeSat supply chain risks.
talks.summary:
The Rise of Rideshare Launches and Secondary Payloads

Modern commercial rockets frequently launch dozens of secondary satellites (CubeSats) alongside primary government and commercial payloads on shared rocket stages.

Threat Modeling the 'Space Hitchhiker' Attack Surface

James Pavur explores untrusted third-party satellites co-located within deployers, analyzing risks of intentional RF jamming, thermal sabotage, or sensor blinding.

Simulating Space-to-Space Radio Exploitation

Pavur presents dynamic simulations demonstrating how a malicious CubeSat in orbit could broadcast spoofed telecommands to compromise nearby high-value satellites.

Policy and Verification Guardrails for Launch Integration

The author proposes technical isolation standards, pre-launch firmware attestation, and regulatory verification to protect rideshare space missions.

talks.title: Defending the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle: Custom Drone IDS
talks.teaser: Jason Whelan presents custom Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) for UAVs, detecting real-time GPS spoofing, signal jamming, and unauthorized telecommands.
talks.summary:
The Inherent Vulnerabilities of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles

Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) rely heavily on unencrypted, unauthenticated wireless signals—including GPS for positioning, ADS-B for collision avoidance, and RF telemetry for C2.

Low-Cost Attacks on Drone Navigation and Control

Jason Whelan reviews practical attack vectors executed using inexpensive software-defined radios (SDRs), covering GPS spoofing, telemetry jamming, and deauthentication.

Designing an Onboard Lightweight Drone IDS

Whelan introduces a lightweight onboard intrusion detection system that correlates flight controller sensor telemetry (IMU, barometer) with incoming GPS signals.

Real-Time Anomaly Detection and Fail-Safe Rerouting

The author demonstrates how the IDS detects navigation manipulation in real time, triggering automated fail-safe return-to-home routines upon detecting GPS spoofing.

talks.title: CPDLC Man-in-the-Middle Attacks in Modern Air Traffic Control
talks.teaser: Joshua Smailes demonstrates injecting forged digital air traffic control messages via CPDLC, executing man-in-the-middle attacks on oceanic flights.
talks.summary:
The Transition to Digital Air Traffic Control Communications

Controller-Pilot Data Link Communications (CPDLC) replaces noisy analog HF/VHF voice communications with direct digital text messaging between pilots and controllers.

The Lack of Cryptographic Authentication in CPDLC

Joshua Smailes analyzes the underlying VDL Mode 2 and ATN protocol stacks, revealing complete absence of message encryption, integrity signing, or mutual authentication.

Executing Airborne Message Injection and Redirection Attacks

Using a software-defined radio, an attacker can broadcast forged ATC clearance messages (such as altitude or route modifications) directly into cockpit flight management systems.

Evaluating Human Detection and Cryptographic Upgrades

Smailes evaluates why flight crews fail to identify subtle forged instructions, presenting proposals for integrating public key infrastructure into future aviation data links.

talks.title: Developing Aerospace Security 3D Training Models
talks.teaser: Kevin Hood shares how developing interactive 3D models and simulated aerospace environments helps students jump-start careers in aerospace cybersecurity.
talks.summary:
The Educational Barrier to Aerospace Cybersecurity

Aspiring aerospace security researchers often face significant hurdles due to the high cost and physical unavailability of real aircraft and satellite hardware.

Engineering Interactive 3D Aerospace Training Models

Kevin Hood demonstrates constructing detailed 3D virtual models and simulated aerospace hardware environments to teach system interactions and attack surfaces.

Simulating Satellite and Aircraft Subsystems

Hood showcases interactive simulations covering spacecraft power distribution, telemetry buses, and flight navigation systems for hands-on student lab exercises.

A Student's Roadmap into Aerospace Cyber Careers

The presentation provides open-source modeling assets and self-guided learning paths for students and educators to build aerospace cyber training curricula.

talks.title: Evaluating Wireless Attacks on Real-World Avionics: GPS & Mode S Spoofing
talks.teaser: Leeloo Granger evaluates wireless attacks on certified Garmin GTN750 avionics hardware, demonstrating live GPS and Mode S spoofing in a certified testbed.
talks.summary:
Validating Theoretical Aviation Vulnerabilities on Real Hardware

While academic literature frequently models wireless attacks on aircraft navigation, testing certified, commercially deployed avionics hardware in lab environments is rare.

Building the Avionics Experimental Testbed

Leeloo Granger presents testing conducted on certified Garmin GTN750 navigators using Software-Defined Radios (USRP B210 and BladeRF).

Executing Live GPS and Mode S Transponder Spoofing

Granger demonstrates generating crafted RF signals to alter cockpit GPS location fixes, trigger false collision alerts (TCAS), and suppress emergency transponder telemetry.

Recommendations for Resilient Airborne Navigation

The author discusses practical mitigations, including multi-constellation GNSS receivers, spatial antenna filtering, and sensor fusion algorithms.

talks.title: Lost in Space: No One Can Hear Your Breach
talks.teaser: Elizabeth Wharton navigates the legal, regulatory, and technical complexities of commercial space cyber breaches, space ransomware, and orbital jurisdiction.
talks.summary:
The Expanding Commercial Space Economy

With privately funded launch providers, commercial satellite mega-constellations, and multinational space stations, the space sector is experiencing exponential growth.

Cyber Threats in the New Space Race

Elizabeth Wharton examines emerging space attack surfaces—including ground station ransomware, supply chain hardware tampering, and orbital satellite command injection.

Navigating Legal and Jurisdictional Ambiguity in Orbit

Wharton analyzes international space treaties (such as the 1967 Outer Space Treaty), discussing liability, national attribution, and insurance complexities when orbital assets are breached.

Establishing International Cyber Norms for Space Operations

The presentation calls for clear international cybersecurity baselines and coordinated incident disclosure frameworks for commercial space operators.

talks.title: Hack-A-Sat 2: The Good, The Bad, and The Cyber Secure
talks.teaser: US Air Force, Space Force, and challenge designers discuss Hack-A-Sat 2, showcasing the physical flatsat satellite hardware used in the world's premier space CTF.
talks.summary:
The Mission Behind the Hack-A-Sat Competition

Hack-A-Sat was created by the US Air Force and US Space Force to bridge the gap between space operators and the global cybersecurity research community.

Inside the Hack-A-Sat 2 Hardware Flatsat

Panelists present the HAS2 flatsat—a modular physical satellite platform integrating real-world space processors, solar sensor arrays, and orbital physics simulators.

Deconstructing Flagship Space Hacking Challenges

The designers review standout competition challenges, including attitude determination tampering, orbital mechanics puzzle solving, and RTOS vulnerability exploitation.

Advancing Space Cybersecurity Through Open Research

The panel reflects on key lessons learned from the competition and invites the broader hacker community to participate in space security research.

talks.title: Unboxing the Spacecraft Software Black Box: Automated Binary Hunting
talks.teaser: Aerospace Corporation lead Brandon Bailey introduces automated binary inspection pipelines to hunt for zero-days in black-box spacecraft firmware.
talks.summary:
The Challenge of Black-Box Spacecraft Firmware

As the commercialization of space accelerates, spacecraft integrators frequently acquire embedded binaries and proprietary flight software without access to source code.

Building Automated Binary Inspection Pipelines

Brandon Bailey details designing automated static and dynamic analysis workflows leveraging Ghidra and custom rule sets tailored to space RTOS binaries.

Hunting for Flaws Across Space Software Architectures

Bailey demonstrates identifying memory corruption bugs, unauthenticated command handlers, and hardcoded encryption keys in compiled flight images.

Accelerating Mission Assurance and Software Verification

The presentation provides spacecraft developers with a scalable, repeatable methodology for pre-flight software security validation.
